## 2B.3 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record points **yes, mostly**. Lula’s security-related posture was repeatedly framed as defensive, institutional, and multilateral: disarmament diplomacy, IAEA-linked oversight, nuclear safety procedures, and dialogue-first crisis management. I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that he manufactured threats, leaned on nationalism/prestige, or used security policy for regime survival. The main counterweights are rhetorical: sharp Gaza language and a Brazil-China Ukraine plan later criticized by Kyiv.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Lula institutionalized disarmament diplomacy rather than using security policy for prestige signaling.
  - **Title:** [Decreto nº 12.237, de 25 de outubro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Presidência da República / Planalto
  - **Date:** October 25, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The decree created Brazil’s permanent delegation to the Conference on Disarmament. That is a concrete multilateral institution-building move, not a manufactured-threat or prestige-based security posture.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s nuclear-security posture in 2024 was explicitly tied to peaceful use and safeguarded oversight.
  - **Title:** [Tratados e regimes com reflexos para a Defesa](https://www.gov.br/defesa/pt-br/assuntos/relacoes-internacionais/foruns-internacionais-1/tratados-e-regimes)
  - **Publisher:** Ministério da Defesa
  - **Date:** Updated 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/defesa/pt-br/assuntos/relacoes-internacionais/foruns-internacionais-1/tratados-e-regimes
  - **Claim-level summary:** The page says Brazil joined the NPT, the Constitution forbids non-peaceful nuclear use, and ABACC subjects the program to independent safeguards. This is strong background evidence that the country’s security posture was defensive rather than nationalist or coercive.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s top security institution reaffirmed technical nuclear-security architecture and support for complete disarmament.
  - **Title:** [GSI/PR participa da IV Conferência Internacional sobre Segurança Física Nuclear](https://www.gov.br/gsi/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/noticias/2024/gsi-pr-participa-da-iv-conferencia-internacional-sobre-seguranca-fisica-nuclear)
  - **Publisher:** Gabinete de Segurança Institucional da Presidência da República
  - **Date:** May 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/gsi/pt-br/centrais-de-conteudo/noticias/2024/gsi-pr-participa-da-iv-conferencia-internacional-sobre-seguranca-fisica-nuclear
  - **Claim-level summary:** Brazil’s delegation reaffirmed the national nuclear-security architecture and said Brazil should resume efforts toward complete nuclear disarmament. This supports a defensive, institution-centered interpretation.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil continued active IAEA-linked cooperation and review in 2024.
  - **Title:** [IAEA recognizes CNEN's "crucial" role in nuclear technology development in Brazil](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** June 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN reported that IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized Brazil’s indispensable cooperation and ongoing collaboration. This is consistent with genuine security needs handled through specialist institutions, not diversionary politics.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Brazil accepted IAEA regulatory self-assessment in 2024, indicating a review-oriented security culture.
  - **Title:** [Brazil participates in unprecedented IAEA self-assessment in Vienna, contributing to strengthening global nuclear safety](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-nuclear-global)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** October 3, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-nuclear-global
  - **Claim-level summary:** Participation in IAEA self-assessment suggests a willingness to subject nuclear governance to external review. That is hard to square with ideology-driven or prestige-only security behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.3`, `1B.7`

- **Claim:** Lula’s 2024 crisis diplomacy repeatedly favored dialogue and ceasefire over force.
  - **Title:** [Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 21, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/21/lula-diz-que-discutiu-conflitos-em-gaza-e-na-ucrania-em-encontro-com-blinken.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula said he discussed peace in Ukraine and Gaza with Antony Blinken, and Planalto reiterated his desire for peace and an end to the conflicts. This supports a defensive, not diversionary, use of crisis politics.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.8`, `2B.1`

- **Claim:** Brazil and China’s Ukraine proposal was framed as negotiation and ceasefire, not threat inflation.
  - **Title:** [Brazil and China sign joint proposal for peace negotiation in the Russia-Ukraine war](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** May 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/05/23/brasil-e-china-assinam-proposta-conjunta-de-negociacao-de-paz-para-guerra-da-ucrania-e-russia.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** The joint statement said dialogue and negotiation were the only viable solution and called for conditions to resume direct talks and move toward a comprehensive ceasefire. That reads as de-escalation, not nationalism or manufactured threat construction.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `2B.1`

### Counterevidence / caveats

- **Claim:** Lula’s Gaza rhetoric was confrontational and caused a diplomatic rupture, which is the clearest 2024 signal of rhetoric that could be read as politically charged rather than strictly defensive.
  - **Title:** [Lula repeats that the Israeli government commits genocide in Gaza and defends the creation of a Palestinian state](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** February 23, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/02/23/lula-repete-que-governo-israelense-comete-genocidio-em-gaza-e-defende-criacao-de-estado-palestino.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Lula repeated the genocide accusation, defended Palestinian statehood, and triggered a major diplomatic rupture with Israel. This is the strongest negative item, but it still looks more like combative moral rhetoric than security manipulation or regime-survival signaling.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.2`, `1B.8`

- **Claim:** Ukraine later criticized the Brazil-China peace initiative as exclusionary and “destructive.”
  - **Title:** [Ukraine's Zelenskiy dismisses 'destructive' China-Brazil peace initiative](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraines-zelenskiy-dismisses-destructive-chinabrazil-peace-initiative-3612966)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
  - **Date:** September 12, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraines-zelenskiy-dismisses-destructive-chinabrazil-peace-initiative-3612966
  - **Claim-level summary:** Zelenskiy said Kyiv was not included and that the plan lacked respect for Ukraine’s territorial integrity. This weakens the initiative’s credibility, but it still does not show a pattern of manufactured threat or diversionary security politics.
  - **Question IDs:** `2B.3`; also `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `2B.1`

### Search gap

I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Lula:
- manufactured security threats for domestic politics,
- used nationalist prestige logic to justify nuclear/security escalation,
- invoked revenge or regime survival motives in security policy,
- or treated genuine defensive needs as a cover for coercion.

The evidence base is mostly the opposite: Brazil’s 2024 security posture was routed through disarmament, safeguards, and multilateral review.
